title: Gravitation
syllabus: The universal law of gravitation; Acceleration due to gravity and its variation with altitude and depth; Kepler's laws of planetary motion; Gravitational potential energy; Gravitational potential; Escape velocity; Orbital velocity of a satellite; Geo-stationary satellites

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The acceleration due to gravity at a height $h$ above the Earth's surface is $g_0/9$, where $g_0$ is the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth. If $R$ is the radius of the Earth, the value of $h$ is:
questions.solution:
The variation of acceleration due to gravity with altitude is given by:
$$g(h) = g_0 \left(\frac{R}{R + h}\right)^2$$
Given $g(h) = \frac{g_0}{9}$:
$$\frac{g_0}{9} = g_0 \left(\frac{R}{R + h}\right)^2 \implies \frac{R}{R + h} = \frac{1}{3} \implies R + h = 3R \implies h = 2R$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A planet has twice the mass and three times the radius of the Earth. If the escape velocity on the surface of the Earth is $v_e$, then the escape velocity on the surface of this planet will be:
questions.solution:
Escape velocity from the surface of a celestial body of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is:
$$v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$$
For the planet with $M' = 2M$ and $R' = 3R$:
$$v'_e = \sqrt{\frac{2G(2M)}{3R}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} v_e$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A satellite is revolving in a circular orbit of radius $r$ around the Earth with speed $v$. If the radius of the orbit is increased to $4r$, its orbital speed will become:
questions.solution:
The orbital speed of a satellite revolving at orbital radius $r$ is:
$$v = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{r}}$$
When the orbital radius increases to $r' = 4r$:
$$v' = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{4r}} = \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{GM}{r}} = \frac{v}{2}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The depth $d$ at which the acceleration due to gravity becomes $\frac{1}{4}$ of its value on the Earth's surface (where $R$ is the radius of the Earth) is:
questions.solution:
The variation of acceleration due to gravity with depth $d$ below the Earth's surface is:
$$g(d) = g_0 \left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right)$$
Given $g(d) = \frac{g_0}{4}$:
$$\frac{g_0}{4} = g_0 \left(1 - \frac{d}{R}\right) \implies 1 - \frac{d}{R} = \frac{1}{4} \implies \frac{d}{R} = \frac{3}{4} \implies d = \frac{3}{4}R$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] A satellite of mass $m$ is revolving in a circular orbit of radius $r$ around the Earth of mass $M$. The total mechanical energy of the satellite is:
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy of the satellite is $K = \frac{1}{2} m v_o^2 = \frac{1}{2} m \left(\frac{GM}{r}\right) = \frac{GMm}{2r}$.
Potential energy is $U = -\frac{GMm}{r}$.
Total mechanical energy:
$$E = K + U = \frac{GMm}{2r} - \frac{GMm}{r} = -\frac{GMm}{2r}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Two spherical bodies of mass $M$ and $5M$ and radii $R$ and $2R$ are released from rest in free space with their centres separated by a distance of $12R$. If they attract each other solely due to gravitational force, the distance moved by the body of mass $M$ just before collision is:
questions.solution:
Because no external force acts on the two-body system, the centre of mass remains stationary.
Initial separation of centres: $d_i = 12R$.
Final separation at collision: $d_f = R + 2R = 3R$.
Total relative displacement between their centres: $\Delta r = 12R - 3R = 9R$.
Displacement of mass $M$ in the centre of mass frame:
$$M \Delta x_1 = 5M \Delta x_2 \implies \Delta x_2 = \frac{\Delta x_1}{5}$$
$$\Delta x_1 + \Delta x_2 = 9R \implies \Delta x_1 + \frac{\Delta x_1}{5} = 9R \implies \frac{6}{5}\Delta x_1 = 9R \implies \Delta x_1 = \frac{45R}{6} = 7.5R$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A body is projected vertically upwards from the surface of the Earth with a speed equal to half the escape velocity. The maximum height attained by the body above the surface of the Earth is (where $R$ is Earth's radius):
questions.solution:
Escape velocity is $v_e = \sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$. The initial launch speed is $v = \frac{v_e}{2} = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{2R}}$.
By conservation of mechanical energy between the surface and highest point ($h$):
$$\frac{1}{2} m v^2 - \frac{GMm}{R} = 0 - \frac{GMm}{R + h}$$
$$\frac{1}{2} m \left(\frac{GM}{2R}\right) - \frac{GMm}{R} = -\frac{GMm}{R + h}$$
$$\frac{1}{4R} - \frac{1}{R} = -\frac{1}{R + h} \implies -\frac{3}{4R} = -\frac{1}{R + h} \implies 3(R + h) = 4R \implies 3h = R \implies h = \frac{R}{3}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The time period of a satellite in a circular orbit of radius $R$ is $T$. The time period of another satellite revolving in an orbit of radius $4R$ around the same central planet will be:
questions.solution:
According to Kepler's third law of planetary motion:
$$T^2 \propto r^3 \implies T \propto r^{3/2}$$
$$\frac{T'}{T} = \left(\frac{4R}{R}\right)^{3/2} = (4)^{3/2} = 8 \implies T' = 8T$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] The gravitational potential $V$ in a region of space is given by $V = (2x - 3y + 4z)\text{ J/kg}$. The magnitude of gravitational field intensity $\vec{E}$ at point $(1, 1, 1)\text{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
Gravitational field intensity is related to gravitational potential by $\vec{E} = -\vec{\nabla} V$:
$$E_x = -\frac{\partial V}{\partial x} = -2, \quad E_y = -\frac{\partial V}{\partial y} = 3, \quad E_z = -\frac{\partial V}{\partial z} = -4$$
$$\vec{E} = -2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$$
Magnitude:
$$|\vec{E}| = \sqrt{(-2)^2 + (3)^2 + (-4)^2} = \sqrt{4 + 9 + 16} = \sqrt{29}\text{ N/kg}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The ratio of acceleration due to gravity at latitude $\lambda = 60^\circ$ to that at the equator due to rotation of the Earth (angular velocity $\omega$, radius $R$) is (taking $g$ as value without rotation):
questions.solution:
The apparent acceleration due to gravity at latitude $\lambda$ due to rotation is:
$$g' = g - \omega^2 R \cos^2\lambda$$
At the equator ($\lambda = 0^\circ$): $g_{\text{eq}} = g - \omega^2 R$.
At latitude $\lambda = 60^\circ$: $\cos 60^\circ = 1/2 \implies \cos^2 60^\circ = 1/4$, so $g_{60} = g - \frac{1}{4}\omega^2 R$.
$$\frac{g_{60}}{g_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{g - \frac{1}{4}\omega^2 R}{g - \omega^2 R}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] Four identical masses $M$ are positioned at the four corners of a square of side $a$. The gravitational potential at the centre of the square is:
questions.solution:
Distance from each corner to the centre of the square of diagonal $a\sqrt{2}$ is $r = \frac{a\sqrt{2}}{2} = \frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$.
Gravitational potential at the centre due to all 4 equal masses is:
$$V_{\text{total}} = 4 \left(-\frac{GM}{r}\right) = 4 \left(-\frac{GM}{a/\sqrt{2}}\right) = -4\sqrt{2} \frac{GM}{a}$$

questions.question: A geostationary satellite orbits around the Earth in a circular path at a distance of approximately $36000\text{ km}$ above the surface. Its period of revolution is:
questions.solution:
A geostationary satellite stays fixed relative to a location on Earth's equator.
Therefore, its period of revolution is equal to Earth's rotational period about its polar axis, which is 1 sidereal day ($24\text{ hours}$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] If the density of a planet is doubled while keeping its radius constant, the acceleration due to gravity on its surface:
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity on the surface of a uniform sphere of radius $R$ and uniform density $\rho$ is:
$$g = \frac{GM}{R^2} = \frac{G \left(\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \rho\right)}{R^2} = \frac{4}{3}\pi G \rho R$$
Because $g \propto \rho$ for constant radius $R$, doubling the density doubles the acceleration due to gravity.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A spaceship is stationed at distance $d$ from the centre of the Earth and distance $r$ from the centre of the Moon. If mass of Earth is $81$ times mass of Moon, the distance of the spaceship from Earth's centre where net gravitational pull is zero is:
questions.solution:
Let $D$ be the distance between centres of Earth and Moon: $d + r = D$.
Equating gravitational forces on mass $m$:
$$\frac{G M_E m}{d^2} = \frac{G M_M m}{r^2} \implies \frac{M_E}{d^2} = \frac{M_M}{r^2}$$
$$\frac{81 M_M}{d^2} = \frac{M_M}{r^2} \implies \frac{9}{d} = \frac{1}{r} \implies d = 9r$$
Substitute $r = D - d$:
$$d = 9(D - d) = 9D - 9d \implies 10d = 9D \implies d = \frac{9}{10} D$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The binding energy of a satellite of mass $m$ revolving in a circular orbit of radius $r$ around the Earth of mass $M$ is:
questions.solution:
The total mechanical energy of the satellite in circular orbit is $E = -\frac{GMm}{2r}$.
Binding energy is the minimum energy required to liberate the satellite to infinity ($E_\infty = 0$):
$$\text{Binding Energy} = -E = +\frac{GMm}{2r}$$

questions.question: A tunnel is dug along a diameter of a uniform solid Earth of mass $M$ and radius $R$. A small coin dropped into the tunnel executes simple harmonic motion. The angular frequency $\omega$ of this motion is:
questions.solution:
At distance $r$ from the centre, gravitational restoring force inside uniform Earth is:
$$F = -\frac{GMm}{R^3} r$$
$$a = \frac{F}{m} = -\left(\frac{GM}{R^3}\right) r$$
Comparing with standard SHM equation $a = -\omega^2 r$:
$$\omega = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{R^3}} = \sqrt{\frac{g}{R}}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A planet moves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit. When the planet is at perihelion (closest distance $r_1$), its speed is $v_1$. When it is at aphelion (farthest distance $r_2$), its speed $v_2$ is:
questions.solution:
Because the gravitational force from the Sun is a central force, the torque on the planet about the Sun is zero.
Angular momentum about the Sun is conserved:
$$L = m v_1 r_1 = m v_2 r_2 \implies v_2 = v_1 \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] The work done to raise a mass $m$ from the surface of the Earth to a height $h = R$ above the surface is (where $g$ is surface gravity and $R$ is Earth's radius):
questions.solution:
Work done equals the gain in gravitational potential energy:
$$W = \Delta U = U_f - U_i = -\frac{GMm}{R + h} - \left(-\frac{GMm}{R}\right)$$
For $h = R$:
$$W = -\frac{GMm}{2R} + \frac{GMm}{R} = \frac{GMm}{2R} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{GM}{R^2}\right) m R = \frac{1}{2} mgR$$

questions.question: If the distance between the Earth and the Sun were halved, the duration of a year on Earth would become approximately:
questions.solution:
By Kepler's third law, $T \propto r^{3/2}$.
If $r' = r/2$:
$$T' = T \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3/2} = \frac{T}{2\sqrt{2}} = \frac{365}{2.828} \approx 129.04\text{ days}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A particle is at the centre of a uniform spherical shell of mass $M$ and radius $R$. The gravitational potential at a point located at distance $R/2$ from the centre is:
questions.solution:
Inside a uniform spherical shell of mass $M$ and radius $R$, the gravitational field is zero everywhere.
Consequently, the gravitational potential inside is uniform and equal to its value on the outer surface:
$$V = -\frac{GM}{R}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is $11.2\text{ km/s}$. A body is launched from the Earth with a speed equal to three times the escape speed ($v = 3 v_e$). Find its speed (in $\text{km/s}$) when it escapes to infinity (take $\sqrt{2} = 1.414$, rounded to one decimal place).
questions.solution:
By conservation of mechanical energy between Earth surface and infinity:
$$\frac{1}{2} m v^2 - \frac{GMm}{R} = \frac{1}{2} m v_\infty^2 + 0$$
Since $\frac{GMm}{R} = \frac{1}{2} m v_e^2$:
$$v_\infty^2 = v^2 - v_e^2 = (3v_e)^2 - v_e^2 = 8 v_e^2$$
$$v_\infty = \sqrt{8} v_e = 2\sqrt{2} (11.2) = 2.8284 \times 11.2 \approx 31.68\text{ km/s} \approx 31.7\text{ km/s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the Earth is $9.8\text{ m/s}^2$. If the radius of the Earth contracts by $1\%$ while its mass remains constant, the percentage increase in the value of $g$ on the surface is $x\%$. Find the value of $x$.
questions.solution:
Acceleration due to gravity on the surface: $g = \frac{GM}{R^2}$.
Taking fractional differences for small percentage variations ($M$ constant):
$$\frac{\Delta g}{g} \approx -2 \frac{\Delta R}{R}$$
Given $\frac{\Delta R}{R} = -1\%$:
$$\frac{\Delta g}{g} \approx -2(-1\%) = +2\%$$
Hence, the percentage increase is $2.0\%$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A satellite of mass $m = 250\text{ kg}$ revolves around the Earth in a circular orbit at a height equal to Earth's radius ($h = R$). The orbital speed of the satellite is $v_o$. If $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$ and $R = 6.4 \times 10^6\text{ m}$, find the orbital speed $v_o$ (in $\text{km/s}$, rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Orbital radius is $r = R + h = 2R$.
Orbital velocity formula:
$$v_o = \sqrt{\frac{GM}{2R}} = \sqrt{\frac{g R^2}{2R}} = \sqrt{\frac{g R}{2}}$$
$$v_o = \sqrt{\frac{10 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{2}} = \sqrt{32 \times 10^6} = \sqrt{3.2 \times 10^7} = 4000\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$$
$$v_o = 4000 \times 1.4142 = 5656.85\text{ m/s} \approx 5.66\text{ km/s}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] Two point masses of $10\text{ kg}$ each are separated by a distance of $1\text{ m}$. Find the magnitude of work done (in Joules) by an external agent in increasing their separation from $1\text{ m}$ to $2\text{ m}$ (take $G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$, express answer in units of $10^{-10}\text{ J}$, rounded to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Gravitational potential energy of two point masses separated by distance $r$ is $U(r) = -\frac{G m_1 m_2}{r}$.
Work done by external agent:
$$W_{\text{ext}} = U(r_2) - U(r_1) = -\frac{G m_1 m_2}{r_2} - \left(-\frac{G m_1 m_2}{r_1}\right) = G m_1 m_2 \left(\frac{1}{r_1} - \frac{1}{r_2}\right)$$
Substitute values:
$$W_{\text{ext}} = (6.67 \times 10^{-11})(10)(10) \left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\right) = 6.67 \times 10^{-9} \times 0.5 = 3.335 \times 10^{-9}\text{ J} = 33.35 \times 10^{-10}\text{ J}$$
*(Expressing as $3.34 \times 10^{-9}\text{ J}$; in $10^{-10}\text{ J}$ it is $33.35$)*
Recalculating value: $(6.67 \times 10^{-9}) \times 0.5 = 3.335 \times 10^{-9}\text{ J} = 3.34\text{ nJ}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An artificial satellite is placed in a circular orbit around the Earth at height $h = R/2$ above the surface, where $R = 6400\text{ km}$ is the radius of the Earth. If the time period of revolution is expressed as $T = k\pi\text{ seconds}$ where $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, find the value of $k$ (take $\sqrt{1.5} \approx 1.225$ and round $k$ to the nearest whole integer).
questions.solution:
Radius of circular orbit: $r = R + h = \frac{3}{2}R$.
Time period of circular orbit:
$$T = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{r^3}{GM}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{(3R/2)^3}{g R^2}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{27 R}{8 g}}$$
Substitute $R = 6.4 \times 10^6\text{ m}$ and $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$:
$$\frac{27 R}{8 g} = \frac{27 \times 6.4 \times 10^6}{80} = 27 \times 80000 = 2160000$$
$$\sqrt{2160000} = \sqrt{216} \times 100 = 6\sqrt{6} \times 100 \approx 14.6969 \times 100 = 1469.69$$
$$T = 2\pi (1469.69) = 2939.39\pi\text{ seconds}$$
Thus $k = 2939.0$.
